design.summary: Every `cfighter` row in the game is masked tgt.air only, so a carrier can launch a full air group and not one aircraft can touch a target ashore. I researched each of the 17 carrier fighters and split them: 16 get the air-to-ground fit they actually had, and three are deliberately withheld — the F-14A Tomcat (fleet air defence only until LANTIRN reached VF-103 in 1996), the F-8E(FN) Crusader (Aeronavale interceptor, 1964–1999, never given the American Y-pylon strike role), and the Su-33 (its only bombing was FAB-500s over Syria in November 2016, and its row covers e90 onward so arming it would back-date 2016 to 1998). A hard blocker shaped the delivery: eras.js lines 10788–11266 are byte-identical to 11366–11844, a 479-line duplicated block containing all four NATO and both Pact deck-fighter rows, so no anchor inside it can be unique and an edit to the first copy is dead text — I therefore deliver those as one derived pass at the tail of eras.js (the idiom that file already uses three times), which runs after both copies and still feeds generations.js normally. Two further defects surfaced: ai.js `pickAirTarget` routes every cfighter into the gunship branch and hands it an enemy MBT, so the AI has been flying carrier fighters at tanks with AIM-54s (warhead "flak", scored 0.04 against heavy armour), and `gbr_e00_cstealth` has duplicate keys whose later copy renames the F-35B to "(none)". All 37 unarmed carrier-capable airframes are AEW aircraft or troop-lift helicopters and every one of them is correctly unarmed — there is no gap there.

findings.what: eras.js contains a 479-line byte-identical duplicated block (lines 10788-11266 repeated at 11366-11844). It holds nato_e50/e60/e80/e90_cfighter and pact_e60/e80_cfighter plus their weapon rows. The later Object.assign wins, so any edit anchored inside is either ambiguous (the text appears twice) or dead (if applied to the first copy). This is why the six affected aircraft cannot be fixed by editing their rows.

findings.what: Every carrier fighter in the game is air-to-air only. 17 cfighter rows across four factions carry nothing with tgt.ground, so a carrier air group cannot attack land at all.
findings.evidence: js/rules.js:2686 cfighter_n weapons:["aam"]; js/rules.js:2251 cfighter_f weapons:["aam"]; js/rules.js:2734 cfighter_c weapons:["aam"]; js/eras.js:10604 fra_e80_cfighter weapons:["w_e80_nato_fighter"] — and w_e80_nato_fighter/aam are tgt:{ground:0,air:1,sea:0,sub:0}.

findings.what: js/ai.js pickAirTarget() has no branch for role "cfighter": it is not "sead"/"ewair", not "fighter", and not "cas", so it falls into the gunship branch and is handed the nearest enemy MBT or harvester as a COMMANDED attack order. An AIM-54/AMRAAM is warhead "flak", which CFG.DMG scores 0.04 against "heavy" — the AI has been flying every carrier fighter it owns at tanks it cannot scratch. Note the gunship branch never calls a.canTarget().
findings.evidence: js/ai.js:5607 'if (a.def.role === "fighter") {' followed at js/ai.js:5617 by 'if (a.def.role !== "cas") {' ... 'if (!(e.def.harvester || e.armor === "heavy")) continue;'. CFG.DMG at js/config.js:143 gives flak {heavy: 0.04}.

findings.what: gbr_e00_cstealth is written with duplicate object keys. The row starts as an F-35B Lightning with full stats and weapons, then re-declares "name":"(none)", "full" and "desc" at the end of the same object literal. The later keys win, so the game holds a buildable 1720-credit unit literally named "(none)" carrying w_e00_nato_stealthfighter. Whichever the author meant (a real F-35B or a null placeholder), the row currently delivers neither. Out of my stream; not fixed.
findings.evidence: js/eras.js:10564 'gbr_e00_cstealth: { ... name:"F-35B Lightning", ... weapons:["w_e00_nato_stealthfighter"], ... desc:"...it is the only stealth aircraft in the world that can do it." ,"name":"(none)","full":"No British carrier stealth fighter in this period","desc":"The Sea Harrier FA2 left service in 2006..."},'

findings.what: The unarmed carrier aircraft are NOT a gap. All 37 carrier-capable airframes with an empty weapons list are either airborne early warning (14 rows: E-1B Tracer, E-2B/C/C-GroupII/C-2000/D, Skyraider AEW.1, Gannet AEW.3, Sea King AEW.2/2A/ASaC.7, Crowsnest) or troop-lift helicopters (23 rows: UH-1/UH-60/Mi-4/Mi-8/Mi-17/Z-5/Z-8/Z-20 families). Every one is correctly unarmed — a Hawkeye carries nothing and a Chickasaw carries soldiers. No edit is warranted and none is proposed.
findings.evidence: Enumerated by walking balanced object literals in js/rules.js, js/eras.js and js/heavyair.js for cat:"aircraft" with weapons:[] that are carrierCapable:true or picked up at runtime by js/game.js:413 'if (_d.role === "aswhelo" || (_spec && _spec.kind !== "wing")) _d.carrierCapable = true;'. Result: 14 cawacs + 23 transport, 0 others.

if (typeof reindexRoles === "function") reindexRoles();

/* ---- what a deck fighter could do to the beach ----
   Measured before this pass: every cfighter row in the game was masked
   tgt.air only, so a carrier could put a full air group up and not one
   aeroplane on it could touch a target ashore. For most of these airframes
   that is simply wrong. For three of them it is RIGHT, and the three are the
   reason this is a hand-written table and not a loop over the role.

   WITHHELD, deliberately, each one a real gap and not a balance decision:

     nato_e80_cfighter  F-14A Tomcat. Fleet air defence and nothing else for
       the whole of the decade this row covers. The airframe was bomb-capable
       from the 1973 flight trials and the Navy declined to use it - no
       cleared stores, no air-to-ground syllabus, the tasking belonged to the
       A-6 and the A-7. The Bombcat is a LANTIRN fit, and the pods did not
       reach VF-103 and VF-14 until 1996.
     fra_e60_cfighter   F-8E(FN) Crusader. Forty-two aircraft bought in 1964
       and flown by the Aeronavale as pure interceptors with R.530 and
       Sidewinder to 1999. The American F-8E's Y-pylon strike role was never
       part of the French one.
     cfighter_p         Su-33 (in rules.js, so not in this table at all). An
       air defence Flanker. The one and only time the type bombed anything
       was FAB-500s over Syria from Kuznetsov in November 2016 with the
       SVP-24 sight, and that row covers e90 onward - arming it would
       back-date 2016 to 1998.

   Where a nation already had an honest ground round for the era it is REUSED
   rather than duplicated. The Sea Hawk FGA.6's four Hispano and RP-3 rockets
   really are w_e50_gbr_cas; the Aquilon's four HS.404 and rocket pods really
   are w_e50_fra_cas; the SEM's GBU-12 under ATLIS II/PDLCT really is
   w_e90_fra_cas; the Rafale M's AASM really is w_e00_fra_cas.
   gbr_e00_cfighter, the Harrier GR9, already carries w_e00_gbr_cas and is
   skipped by the guard below.

   Two mechanical reasons this lives HERE, at the tail of the file, rather
   than on the unit rows:
     - the NATO and Pact deck-fighter rows are defined TWICE in this file and
       the second definition silently wins, so an edit to the first copy is
       dead text. This runs after both.
     - generations.js has not run yet, so these mounts still go through the
       DOMAIN accuracy pass and the POOL magazine pass like any other weapon.
   Appended and never prepended: generations.js writes u.weapons[0] when it
   substitutes a private clone, so the air-to-air mount has to stay first. */

     dedicated attack version of the same aeroplane. Below nato_e50_cas (139,
     the AD-4 Skyraider) because a Skyraider hauls four times the load. */
  w_e50_nato_cstrike: { name:"HVAR rockets and two 1,000 lb bombs", dmg:112, warhead:"he",

     from a subsonic aeroplane with no attack radar, so accuracy is poor. */

    aoe:2.4, suppress:74, ammo:2, tgt:{ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0} },
  /* Super Etendard, 1978. France's carrier-borne strike aeroplane: 250 kg
     bombs and 68 mm rocket pods conventionally, Exocet against ships, and the
     AN 52 free-fall nuclear weapon and then ASMP from 1988 - the nuclear
     round is not modelled here and is not meant to be. Deliberately NOT
     w_e80_fra_cas, which is the Jaguar's AS.30L under an ATLIS II pod; the
     Super Etendard did not get a laser designator until the SEM rebuild. */
  w_e80_fra_cstrike: { name:"250 kg bombs and 68 mm rocket pods", dmg:186, warhead:"he",
    range:2.0, reload:1.24, burst:2, burstDelay:0.35, acc:0.62, proj:"bomb", speed:0,
    aoe:2.4, suppress:76, ammo:2, tgt:{ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0} },
  /* Yak-38 Forger, 1976. The type was a shturmovik before it was anything
     else - it has no radar, so ground attack is most of what it could
     honestly do - and the payload is the story: about a tonne, two hardpoints

     w_e60_pact_cas, the Su-17M, is 185 for roughly two and a half tonnes.
     This is deliberately less than half of that. */
  w_e60_pact_cstrike: { name:"UB-32 pods or a pair of FAB-250 - a tonne, all told",
    dmg:76, warhead:"he", range:1.6, reload:1.55, burst:2, burstDelay:0.35, acc:0.52,
    proj:"bomb", speed:0, aoe:2.0, suppress:48, ammo:2, tgt:{ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0} },

  w_e80_pact_cstrike: { name:"FAB-250 and UB-32 after a rolling takeoff", dmg:104,
    warhead:"he", range:1.7, reload:1.45, burst:2, burstDelay:0.35, acc:0.56, proj:"bomb",

edits.why: Gives thirteen era carrier fighters the air-to-ground fit they actually flew — Sea Hawk FGA.6 and Phantom FG.1 have ground attack in the designation, the Sea Harrier FRS.1 dropped 1,000 lb retarded bombs and BL755 over Stanley in 1982, the Super Etendard was France's carrier nuclear and Exocet striker from 1978, the F/A-18C bombed and shot down MiG-21s in the same sortie on 17 January 1991, and the Yak-38 was a shturmovik with a one-tonne payload — while withholding it from the F-14A (Bombcat is a LANTIRN fit that reached the fleet in 1996) and the F-8E(FN) (Aeronavale interceptor, 1964–1999). It is placed at the tail of eras.js because the NATO and Pact rows are defined twice in that file and the second copy wins, so there is no unique anchor on those rows and an edit to the first copy would be dead text.

But two of its stated justifications are wrong against the tree the edits will land on, the ai.js edit only does half its own job, and one damage figure says the opposite of the comment above it.

Engine checks performed and passed: (a) none of the nine new rows sets tgt.air, and jdam is tgt:{ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0} with warhead "he", so no inert mount is created; (b) nothing new is proj!=="missile" while masked air, so combat.js:226 areaSam() counts exactly what it counted before; (c) all 13 DECK_STRIKE unit ids and all 13 weapon ids resolve, and the loop guards with `if (!_du || !_du.weapons || !WEAPONS[_dw]) continue`; (d) exact-string counts confirm all five anchors appear once each and the nine new keys appear zero times anywhere in js/; (e) the insertion point at js/eras.js:11422 is top-level scope where UNITS and WEAPONS are the same globals the torpedo and rocket passes below it already use, and it runs before generations.js so the DOMAIN pass (js/generations.js:433-464) and POOL (js/generations.js:901-908, cfighter:5) still see the appended round; (f) appending rather than prepending is right - generations.js:938 states the rule explicitly, and the DOMAIN loop writes u5.weapons[q5] in place so order survives; (g) no pass in generations.js rewrites a cfighter's array wholesale - giveWeapon()'s unshift is gated on role==="cas" only; (h) Unit.pickWeapon() gates on t.targetLayer() before scoring, so the new ground round is unreachable against air targets and the a2a mount is unreachable against ground, which is what makes the two-mount loadout behave; (i) the concat-plus-already-armed-guard is the same idiom generations.js:878-888 uses for the F-35 BAY pass, so the plan is following the file rather than inventing a mechanism; (j) nothing in entities.js, game.js, combat.js or threat.js gates air behaviour on role === "fighter", so a cfighter carrying a bomb flies the bomb pass like any other jet (entities.js:2135 standoff test keys off w.proj, not role).

Realism checks: the three withheld airframes are correctly withheld and none is a balance decision - F-14A had no cleared air-to-ground stores before LANTIRN reached VF-103/VF-14 in 1996; the F-8E(FN) was an Aeronavale interceptor 1964-1999 and never got the American Y-pylon role; cfighter_p carries from:"e90" so arming the Su-33 would back-date November 2016 to 1998. cfighter_k exists only as 3D art in js/air_specs.js:81 and js/units3d_air2.js:436 and has no UNITS row, which is consistent with the no-KPA-carrier position. The reuse of w_e50_gbr_cas, w_e50_fra_cas, w_e90_fra_cas and w_e00_fra_cas rather than duplicating them is correct and the DOMAIN pass clones per-unit where it scales, so no shared row is mutated (at e50 DOMAIN_BITE is 0.00, so acc===1 && rng===1 and the loop does not even clone).

The plan's minor finding about gbr_e00_cstealth is real and still present in the working tree: the object literal closes with ,"name":"(none)","full":"No British carrier stealth fighter in this period","desc":"..." after a full F-35B row, so the later keys win. What does not hold up is listed in fatals.

fatals.problem: The ai.js edit's `why` and the finding it rests on describe a mechanism the engine does not have. It claims the AI "fires a flak-warhead missile scored 0.04 against heavy armour" and "has been flying every carrier fighter it owns at tanks it cannot scratch [with] AIM-54s". Unit.pickWeapon() (js/entities.js:1507-1558) gates every mount on the target's presented layer BEFORE it scores anything - `if (tl === "ground" && !w.tgt.ground) continue;` at js/entities.js:1537 - so a cfighter carrying only tgt.air rounds skips every mount and returns -1. The attack branch of updateAir then reads `const wi = this.pickWeapon(t); ... if (wi < 0) { this.order = this.afterAttack(o); return; }` (js/entities.js:2127-2129) and abandons the order on the same tick. fatals.correction: Keep the edit; correct the claim. fatals.problem: The ai.js edit fixes only half the loop it describes. Making pickAirTarget() return null for an air-to-air-only deck fighter drops the aircraft through to the sweep fallback in the sortie loop, which reads `a.give(a.def.role === "fighter" ? { type: "cap", ... } : { type: "attackmove", ... });` at js/ai.js:4317-4319. Role is "cfighter", not "fighter", so the F-14A, the F-8E(FN) Crusader and the Su-33 - the three aircraft the edit exists to rescue - are still sent on an armed attackmove at the objective instead of taking station on CAP. That is the interceptor behaviour the edit's own comment claims to restore, and it is left unrestored. (The withheld fighters will now reach this line MORE often, not less, because pickAirTarget returns null wherever it previously returned an MBT.)

fatals.problem: Placement bug. The replacement emits `Object.assign(WEAPONS, {...})` AFTER the anchor line, i.e. after reindexRoles() has already run. js/rules.js:4249, inside reindexRoles(), is what stamps every weapon's own key onto it: `for (var _w in WEAPONS) WEAPONS[_w].id = _w;`. The nine new *_cstrike rows would be the only weapons in the game with no .id. Impact is small but real and free to avoid: js/audio.js:198 and :234 read `w.id` (they fall back to w.name, so today it only degrades the synthesised weapon sound's cache key), and any future reader of WEAPONS[k].id silently gets undefined for exactly these nine rows.
fatals.correction: Emit the entire inserted block BEFORE the anchor line rather than after it: replacement = <the whole new comment + Object.assign(WEAPONS,{...}) + the DECK_STRIKE IIFE> followed by a blank line and then `if (typeof reindexRoles === "function") reindexRoles();`. This is strictly better and costs nothing: the last cfighter row (pact_e80_cfighter) is at line 11177 and the anchor is at 11422, so the DECK_STRIKE pass still runs after every unit definition, and the nine new weapons now get their .id stamped like every other row.

fatals.problem: The ai.js guard reads `(a.def.role === "cfighter" || a.def.role === "cstealth")`, but this plan arms no cstealth row anywhere. Verified: cstealth_n (F-35C, js/rules.js:2699), cstealth_b (F-35B, js/rules.js:3241) and cstealth_c (J-35, js/rules.js:2740) all carry weapons:["aam_lo"] and nothing else; gbr_e00_cstealth (js/eras.js:10614) carries only w_e00_nato_stealthfighter. All four are air-to-air only. So after this pass SEVEN carrier rows remain ground-incapable, not three, and measurement request #1's stated expectation — "exactly three cfighter/cstealth rows remain ground-incapable" — cannot pass; the orchestrator will read a correct run as a failure. It also quietly locks the F-35B/C and J-35, strike fighters by design, into interceptor-only AI routing forever.
fatals.correction: Pick one and be explicit. Minimal and safest for this stream: drop `|| a.def.role === "cstealth"` so the guard reads `const deckA2A = a.def.role === "cfighter" && !(a.def.weapons || []).some(...)`, leaving cstealth behaviour exactly as it is today, and note the four unarmed cstealth rows as an out-of-stream gap in the findings. If instead you keep cstealth in the guard (defensible — an aam_lo at 0.04 against heavy armour is a wasted sortie either way), then rewrite measurement #1 to expect SEVEN ground-incapable rows — nato_e80_cfighter, fra_e60_cfighter, cfighter_p, cstealth_n, cstealth_b, cstealth_c, gbr_e00_cstealth — and say in the finding that the F-35/J-35 strike fit is a known remaining gap, not a deliberate withholding.

fatals.problem: Minor, both in this edit and in edit 4: the ground-capability test is `_dwp.tgt && _dwp.tgt.ground` (and `WEAPONS[k].tgt && WEAPONS[k].tgt.ground` in ai.js), which is stricter than the engine's own rule. js/entities.js:1535 gates only inside `if (w.tgt) { ... }`, so a mount with NO tgt field can hit anything, ground included. A weapon like that would be judged air-only by both new tests — the eras.js guard would bolt a second bomb onto a unit that already strikes, and the ai.js guard would fly a ground-capable aircraft as an interceptor.
fatals.correction: Match the engine in both places: use `if (_dwp && (!_dwp.tgt || _dwp.tgt.ground)) { _had = true; break; }` in the eras.js loop and `.some(k => WEAPONS[k] && (!WEAPONS[k].tgt || WEAPONS[k].tgt.ground))` in ai.js. No live row is affected today — every cfighter and cstealth mount I checked has an explicit tgt — so this is cheap insurance, not a bug being fixed.
